Thanks for the details — that helps a lot. Quick, high-level sizing notes (back-of-envelope based on Redwood serving profiles for chat-style workloads at ~1k token context):
- Baseline assumption: H100-equivalent GPU with optimized kernels, mixed-precision quantization for gen path. We size for 220 token responses on average.
- Single GPU baseline throughput (conservative): ~10–12 requests/sec at ~1k context while meeting p95 ~600–800ms depending on batching.
- Given your peaks (85 r/s spikes), sustained 30 r/s, concurrency 25–40: recommend a pool that can sustain 30 r/s steady and absorb spikes to ~85 r/s with short burst capacity.

Recommended starting configuration (US launch):
- Committed pool: 6x H100-equivalent GPUs (this yields steady-state capacity ~60–72 r/s in conservative config with prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching).
- Burst capacity: allow 2x burst headroom (automatic burst to on-demand capacity) to absorb short spikes to ~120–140 r/s — Redwood can route excess to on-demand pool with graceful degradation policy.
- Concurrency: with 6 GPUs and progressive batching, expect median in-flight concurrency 30–45; recommend setting request queue depth to cap tail latencies and enable priority preemption for interactive flows.

Cost/commit recommendation:
- 12-month reserved commit at 35% off list for the 6-GPU pool (we can firm exact MSRP in the formal quote).
- 24-month commit: additional 5–8% discount depending on advanced payment and reference allowance.
- Include 1-week onboarding credits and 3 days of SRE assistance for launch tuning in the package.

Caveats & tuning levers:
- If you can shorten average context by pruning history (or rely on lightweight retrieval), each GPU can serve more concurrent requests; every ~200 tokens reduced in context roughly improves throughput ~8–12% in our tests.
- Embeddings traffic we recommend routing to a smaller, separate pool to avoid interfering with chat tail latencies.

I've attached a sizing workbook with conservative / expected / optimistic scenarios (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v2.xlsx). Happy to run a more precise sim if you share a 48-hour sample trace.

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
